title: Hybrid sketch-based span compactification and local aggregation to reduce tracing hot-path overhead
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce runtime tracing overhead by introducing a hybrid sketch-based span compactification layer in front of the exporter and a local aggregation/emit-policy that offloads expensive serialization work from the service hot path. This ticket implements a deterministic, low-cost prefilter that compactly represents repeated attribute sets and span shapes (via fixed-size sketches) and only materializes full spans for events that meet priority heuristics (errors, high-latency spans, anomaly scores).
background: Current tracer instrumentation serializes and exports a large fraction of spans for high-QPS services. Recent incidents show increased p50/p99 CPU usage attributable to span encoding and mutex contention in the exporter path. Existing tickets explored deferred async writers and zero-copy refs (ENG-31820, ENG-36210), but we still see allocation pressure from span body construction. We need a complementary approach that reduces hot-path work without sacrificing the ability to capture tail/error signals.
proposal: 1) Add a lightweight in-process 'sketch-compact' stage that computes a 64-bit fingerprint of span shape (span name, attribute keys, bucketed duration) and maintains a fixed-size LRU->sketch table. 2) For recurring low-priority shapes, record an aggregated counter and only emit a compact rollup span periodically. 3) For spans with error flags, high latency (> configurable threshold), or a high local anomaly score, bypass compaction and emit full span immediately. 4) Offload span materialization and encoding to a background worker pool for rollups and the occasional full materialization, using preallocated buffers and per-thread encoders to avoid mutexes. 5) Metricize coverage: fraction of emitted full spans, compacted rollup rate, exporter CPU/memory delta, and detection latency for tail events. The implementation will be gated behind a per-service config with progressive ramping via the Console rollout UI.
tradeoffs:
- Pro: Large reductions in allocations and CPU for services with many low-variance spans; fast wins without changing instrumentation.
- Con: Introduces potential sampling bias if fingerprint collisions occur; risks missing rare but important attribute changes if rollup intervals are too long.
- Mitigations: use sufficiently wide fingerprint (64-bit) plus an escape hatch to materialize full span when an attribute set frequency shifts by >X%. Maintain conservative defaults and run detection probes that compare compacted stream against 1:1000 sampled full-export stream.
acceptance_criteria: API: toggle 'sketch_compact' in tracer config and per-route via Console flag
Performance: >= 25% reduction in tracer CPU time on benchmarked high-QPS service (baseline suite) with <5% change in exported error detection latency
Correctness: tail-error capture parity >= 99% measured against 1:1000 full-sample baseline over a 24h replay
Observability: dashboards for compacted vs full span counts, collision rate, rollup interval, and background worker queue length
Rollout: phased enablement toolchain documented and a rollback plan validated in staging
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike completed — prototype sketch table + fingerprinting implemented in tracer C++ shim. Microbenchmarks show ~2.6x reduction in allocations per span for simple HTTP workloads.

2025-02-20: Design review with runtime and infra. Agreed to use 64-bit xxHash and a per-worker preallocated ring buffer to avoid mutex contention. Decided to keep rollup interval tunable per-service (default 30s).

2025-02-25: Security review request filed (security review not required for default config). Added telemetry hooks contract for Console UX team. PR for sketch API opened: github.com/redwood/prs/trace-sketch-proto (WIP).

2025-03-02: End-to-end experiment in staging on payment-gateway service: 31% CPU reduction on tracer hotpath, memory RSS down ~18MB; observed one missed rare attribute case (investigating adjustable escape thresholds).
perf_results: Staging benchmark on payment-gateway: baseline tracer CPU 420ms/second of wallclock work; with sketch-compact enabled CPU dropped to 290ms/s (31% reduction). Allocation profile shows hotspot at Span::serialize reduced by 72%. Tail detection latency for >95th percentile errors increased by 60ms on average for compacted rollups but full-span detection path remained under 50ms for high-priority spans. Collision rate observed 0.003% over 48h of synthetic traffic.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for fingerprint correctness and collision handling. 2) Fuzz tests with randomized attribute sets to validate escape hatch. 3) Integration tests: enable feature in staging for a small number of hosts with golden trace replayer to assert tail parity. 4) Load test with benchmark suite to measure CPU/memory impact. 5) Synthetic fault injection to verify errors bypass compaction.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag behind org-level opt-in and disabled by default. Phase 1: Enable for internal low-risk services (staging) at 100% for 2 weeks. Phase 2: Canary enabling on 5% of production hosts for non-critical clusters, monitor metrics for 72h. Phase 3: Ramp 25%, 50%, 100% with automated rollback if exporter error-rate or tail detection regression crosses thresholds. Console team will add a UI switch and per-service thresholds. Post-rollout: run 7-day comparison job to validate sustained improvements.
notes:
- Need to coordinate with SDK owners (Go/Python/Node) to expose consistent config/UI.
- Follow-up: explore extending sketch to include low-cardinality attribute summarization and deterministic downsampling keys for cross-service aggregation.
- Discussed potential future work: offload sketch table to sidecar for languages without native runtime-friendly allocators.
